name: update_returned_structure_field
description: Calls a function taken from a pointer table inside the structure passed as the first argument, passing that structure, then stores the second argument into a field of the structure that call returns. It returns nothing.

name: call_setup_with_rollback
description: Calls a first routine with the last two arguments and, if it gives a non-zero result, passes that result to a second routine together with the first two arguments. If the second routine returns zero, the result is passed to a third routine and zero is returned; otherwise the first result is returned.

name: load_record_from_buffer
description: Obtains a record through the first routine and has the second routine fill a 44-byte stack buffer. On success it copies the buffer and several fields into the record, links the record into a parent record when one is set, and returns it; if the fill fails it passes the record to a third routine and returns zero.

name: copy_record_fields_from_frame
description: Copies 44 bytes and several fields from a stack frame into a record whose address is held in a register, and links the record into a parent when one is set.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero immediately, with no other work.

name: build_record_request_buffer
description: Copies 44 bytes and several fields from the record passed as the third argument into a stack buffer, places a fixed two-word header at its start, and passes that buffer with the first two arguments to another routine.

name: load_info_icon_file
description: Reads a file named with the .info extension: it checks a signature and version in the header, then reads its data blocks into newly allocated memory. It returns one on success and zero on failure, and releases the file handle before returning.

name: read_info_icon_blocks
description: Checks a signature and version in the header, clears two fields, then reads two values into the record and, depending on its flags, reads table and data blocks into newly allocated memory. It returns one on success and zero on failure.

name: read_icon_block_tables
description: Reads two values into fields of the record, then reads optional pointer tables and a data block into allocated memory. It returns one on success and zero on failure.

name: read_table_entries_until_done
description: Reads 4-byte entries into an array, decreasing a byte count until it runs out, then reads one optional data block into allocated memory. It returns one on success and zero on failure.

name: forward_call_return_zero
description: Calls one other routine with no arguments and then returns zero.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without doing anything.

name: transfer_icon_with_temp_buffer
description: Allocates a 260-byte work area, transfers a 78-byte header and then optional list and data blocks through the library, and frees the work area before returning. It saves one field of the record beforehand, restores it at the end, and returns one on success or zero on failure.

name: transfer_info_icon_contents
description: Transfers the contents of a file named with the .info extension: a 78-byte header followed by optional list and data blocks. It saves one record field before the transfer, restores it afterwards, and returns one on success or zero on failure.

name: write_length_prefixed_entries
description: Writes an optional pointer table in which each entry is preceded by its length plus one, then an optional data block. It restores a record field afterwards and returns one on success or zero on failure.

name: write_record_string_table
description: Adds up the sizes of a null-terminated pointer list, then writes each entry of the record's table preceded by its length plus one, followed by an optional data block. It returns one on success or zero on failure.

name: write_pointer_list_entries
description: Walks a null-terminated list of pointers and writes each entry, preceded by its length plus one, through the library. It then writes an optional data block and returns one on success or zero on failure.

name: release_list_items_in_record
description: Repeatedly takes the next item from a list held in the record and passes it to a release routine, until the list returns nothing.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without doing anything.

name: forward_call_with_offset
description: Calls another routine with the same first argument and the second argument increased by 140, then returns.

name: allocate_and_fill_record
description: Allocates a 168-byte record and calls one routine to obtain a field of it. If that succeeds, it passes the record to a second routine to fill it and returns the record; if the first routine fails, it frees the record and returns zero.

name: forward_call_and_return
description: Calls one other routine with no arguments and then returns, doing nothing else.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero immediately, with no other work.

name: refill_and_store_pair
description: Refills a counter through a routine when it has reached zero, decrements it, and stores two 32-bit values into the table slot it indexes. It returns one on success and zero if the refill fails.

name: decrement_counter_and_store_pair
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter through a pointer, then stores two 32-bit values into the table slot that the counter indexes, and returns one.

name: allocate_record_with_cleanup
description: Allocates a 94-byte record, calls one routine to obtain a field of it, and then calls a second routine to fill the record. If any step fails it releases what was allocated and returns zero; otherwise it returns the record.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without doing anything.

name: forward_call_return_zero
description: Calls one other routine with no arguments and then returns zero.

name: forward_call_with_offset
description: Calls another routine with the same first argument and the second argument increased by 78, then returns.

name: find_value_after_equals
description: Walks a null-terminated list of pointers, passing each entry and the second argument to another routine, and returns a pointer to the character after an equals sign in the first entry that matches. It returns zero if the list ends without a match.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero immediately, with no other work.

name: match_delimited_segment
description: Scans text whose segments are separated by the character with code 124, comparing each segment's length with the given length and calling a comparison routine on matches. It returns one when a segment matches and zero when none does.

name: scan_segments_for_match
description: Scans text whose segments are separated by the character with code 124, returning one when a segment has the expected length and the comparison routine reports a match, and zero otherwise.

name: scan_segments_for_match
description: Scans text whose segments are separated by the character with code 124, returning one when a segment has the expected length and the comparison routine reports a match, and zero otherwise.

name: scan_segments_for_match
description: Scans text whose segments are separated by the character with code 124, returning one when a segment has the expected length and the comparison routine reports a match, and zero otherwise.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero immediately, with no other work.

name: build_copy_name_string
description: Builds a display name in a 31-byte buffer: it writes either a plain 'copy' prefix or a numbered 'copy N of' prefix, depending on the source text, followed by up to 30 characters of the name. The last byte of the buffer is set to zero first.

name: parse_copy_number_text
description: Parses decimal digits at a fixed offset in the record, checks a fixed-length item after the digits, and runs two cleanup calls before returning. The parsed value is not returned.

name: parse_decimal_number_text
description: Parses a run of decimal digits from the text passed in, then checks a fixed-length item after them. It runs two cleanup calls and returns nothing.

name: parse_copy_count_digits
description: Parses a run of decimal digits, then checks a fixed-length item after them, and returns nothing after two cleanup calls. The text fragments ' of ' and 'copy %ld of ' suggest it handles copy counts written in names.

name: convert_char_to_digit
description: Converts a character code from 48 to 57 into its digit value from 0 to 9, and returns -1 for any other character.

name: call_setup_with_rollback
description: Calls a first routine with the last two arguments and, if it gives a non-zero result, passes that result to a second routine together with the first two arguments. If the second routine returns zero, the result is passed to a third routine and zero is returned; otherwise the first result is returned.

name: allocate_and_initialize_record
description: Allocates a 96-byte record, sets a size field inside it and a word in the caller's buffer to ten, then passes the record and the address one word past the buffer to another routine. It returns true when the allocation succeeded.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero immediately, with no other work.

name: verify_result_matches
description: Calls one routine with the last three arguments and returns the fourth argument if the routine returned that same value, otherwise zero.

name: return_without_action

name: verify_result_matches
description: Calls one routine with the last three arguments and returns the fourth argument if the routine returned that same value, otherwise zero.

name: return_without_action

name: divide_unsigned_32bit
description: Divides a 32-bit unsigned value by a 32-bit divisor and returns the quotient and remainder together in one 64-bit result. Divisors above 65535 use a 16-step shift-and-subtract loop, while smaller divisors use direct 16-bit divide steps.

name: divide_32bit_shift_loop
description: Runs the 16-step shift-and-subtract division loop on a value and divisor held in registers, leaving the quotient and the remainder in two registers. It is the same loop that the large-divisor branch of the division routine before it contains.

name: multiply_low_32_bits
description: Multiplies two 32-bit register inputs using cross products of their 16-bit halves and returns the low 32 bits of the product, with the second input passed back as the other word.

name: call_raw_format_routine
description: Calls the Amiga text-formatting routine through a function pointer read from a fixed offset in a global structure, then returns. The facts list the library call as RawDoFmt, which passes each formatted character to a small copy routine.

name: measure_string_length
description: Counts the characters before the terminating zero byte of a string and returns that count.

name: find_character_in_string
description: Searches a null-terminated string for the given character and returns a pointer to its first occurrence, or zero if it is not present.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero immediately, with no other work.

name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies bytes from the source string into the destination, including the terminating zero byte.

name: append_string_to_string
description: Finds the end of the first string and copies the second string, including its terminating zero byte, onto that position.

name: compare_strings_up_to_limit
description: Compares two byte strings for at most the given number of characters. It returns one as soon as a byte differs, and zero if the strings match up to the limit or the terminating zero byte.

name: return_one_stub
description: Returns one immediately, with no other work.

name: scan_string_up_to_limit
description: Walks a string for at most the given number of characters, calling another routine when it reaches the terminating zero byte before the limit runs out.

name: forward_call_and_return
description: Calls one other routine with no arguments and then returns, doing nothing else.

name: copy_string_and_pad
description: Copies a null-terminated string into a destination of the given size, stopping after the terminating zero byte, and then fills the remaining bytes with zeros.

name: initialize_list_header
description: Writes a head pointer four bytes past the start of the block, clears the word that follows it, and stores the block's own address eight bytes in. It sets up a list header inside the given block.

name: process_entry_with_status
description: If the argument is non-zero, calls one routine on it with size 20. If that succeeds, it calls two routines and passes a field of the argument, together with the result, to a third routine. It returns the status, which is one when the argument is zero.

name: walk_entry_list
description: Walks a linked list of entries through the next pointer at offset 12. For each entry it calls one routine with size 16, then calls another on the data pointer at offset 8 with a size taken from the byte at offset 7 times four; it returns zero if a call fails and one when the list ends.

name: return_one_stub
description: Returns one immediately, with no other work.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero immediately, with no other work.

name: allocate_and_transfer_record
description: Returns zero when the fourth argument is zero. Otherwise it allocates a 20-byte record, passes it to one routine with the third argument, then reads a two-unit value into the record at offset 10 and passes it to a final routine. It returns the record on success and -1 on failure.

name: return_minus_one_stub
description: Returns minus one immediately, with no other work.

name: load_entry_list
description: Allocates and reads a linked list of entries, each consisting of a 16-byte header and a data block whose size is the byte at offset 7 times four. Entries are linked through the next pointer at offset 12, and the routine returns the first entry on success or -1 if any step fails.

name: read_entry_list_links
description: Loops over the entries of a list, reading each entry's data pointer and size and linking the next entry through offset 12. It returns the first entry, or -1 when any read fails.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without doing anything.

name: return_minus_one_stub
description: Returns minus one immediately, with no other work.

name: copy_sixteen_words_and_call
description: When the first argument is non-zero, copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed offset in the data record into it. It then calls a routine through a function pointer held in a register.

name: clear_data_and_start
description: Program entry point: it clears a block of about 32 kilobytes in the data area, saves the stack pointer and the library base in it, and calls a library routine if a flag bit is set. It then calls a setup routine, or the next routine if setup returns zero.

name: initialize_game_libraries
description: Stores two values obtained from routines into the data area, then calls several setup routines and passes the stored values on. The text it references names graphics.library, intuition.library, the save area and the data file.

name: copy_file_in_blocks
description: Copies a file in blocks of at most 32,768 bytes from a source file to a destination file, opening both through the file system. If a write fails it closes both handles and shows an error message; the text references include 'Disk full', 'Unable to create file' and 'Unable to open file'.

name: write_buffer_in_blocks
description: Writes a buffer to an open file in blocks of at most 32,768 bytes, checking the size actually written for each block. On a short write it closes the file and shows an error message.

name: check_battlechess_directory
description: Locks a path built from a prefix and the name BattleChess with read access, unlocks it, and locks it again. It stores the outcome as a flag and calls a routine with 512 and 2 and that flag, storing the result in a data field.

name: update_handle_and_delay
description: When a handle stored at a fixed offset is set and the argument is non-zero, passes the handle and the argument through several routines and then waits a fixed delay of 250 units. It also performs a few routine calls with fixed arguments in every case.

name: draw_transfer_progress_screen
description: Opens a display handle stored in the data area, then draws a series of graphic elements and text labels at fixed positions. The text it references includes 'Transferring', 'Bytes transferred' and the ChessToDH0 name, and it has no return value.

name: close_handle_if_open
description: If the handle stored at a fixed offset in the data area is set, passes it to a library routine and clears the stored value.

name: draw_display_element
description: Draws a label or value on the display handle stored at a fixed offset, using a series of positioning and drawing calls. It passes its argument through a routine to produce the text it draws.

name: add_to_counter_and_draw
description: Adds the argument to a counter stored in the data area, then draws a value on the display handle using the results of two routine calls.

name: forward_call_with_argument
description: Calls another routine with its single argument and then returns.

name: initialize_disk_port
description: Sets up disk access state in the data area: it creates a message port and, if that fails, opens trackdisk.device using a 56-byte I/O request. If setup fails, it reports a fatal error message; the text references include 'unable to create port' and 'unable to access the specified drive'.

name: store_two_values_in_record
description: Stores its two arguments into fields of the data area and clears a third field to zero.

name: store_value_and_clear_field
description: Stores its argument into one field of the data area and clears another field to zero.

name: transfer_data_in_sectors
description: Copies a buffer in 512-byte sectors through a routine: it first fills the rest of the current sector, then whole sectors, then any final partial sector. It updates the position and count fields as it goes.

name: transfer_sectors_from_position
description: Converts the current position into a sector number by dividing by 512, obtains a starting address through a routine, and transfers whole 512-byte sectors one at a time while the count is positive.

name: copy_sector_blocks
description: Repeatedly calls a routine on two pointers, advancing each by one 512-byte block and reducing the remaining count, until the count is no longer positive.

name: release_disk_handles
description: Releases the disk handle stored in the data area when it is set. If that handle is clear but a second handle is set, it calls two routines and then releases the second handle with its request block.

name: seek_and_read_sector
description: Sets the buffer position from the offset within a 512-byte sector. With an open file handle it seeks to the sector start and reads 512 bytes; without one it computes a sector number, adjusts it past a fixed limit, and loads that sector through a routine only when it differs from the last one loaded.

name: start_sector_read_request
description: Fills in a request block for a 512-byte read at the sector given by the first argument, setting the command word and the buffer address from the second argument, and passes the block to a routine to start the request.

name: start_sector_write_request
description: Fills in a request block for a 512-byte write at the sector given by the first argument, setting the command word and the buffer address from the second argument, and passes the block to a routine to start the request.

name: wait_for_data_disk
description: Checks a status byte and, while it holds a specific value, shows the 'Insert the Battle Chess data disk.' prompt and waits before checking again. It repeats until the status byte is zero.

name: check_battle_chess_file
description: Saves a 56-byte request block, sends a request built from the data area, and if the status byte is zero checks a file named Battle Chess through a routine. It restores the saved block in every case and returns one when that routine returned zero.

name: send_disk_control_request
description: Sets the command word of the request block to a fixed control value and passes the block to a routine.

name: send_disk_control_if_idle
description: If the handle at a fixed offset is zero, sets the request command to a fixed value of nine with a zero length and passes the block to a routine.

name: invalidate_sector_cache
description: Marks the cached sector number as invalid by setting it to minus one, then returns the value stored in another field of the data area.

name: build_message_buffer
description: Clears a 132-byte stack buffer, copies its argument into the buffer from offset 3, sets bytes 1 and 2 to fixed values, and passes the buffer to an output routine with a length of 32.

name: fill_memory_with_byte
description: Writes one byte value into consecutive bytes of the target area for the given count. It returns nothing.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without doing anything.

name: initialize_dos_context
description: Allocates a block sized from a data field, initializes its header fields, and stores a four-byte tag in the data area. It then queries the current directory and the standard input and output through the DOS library, opening a file when the stored handle is not yet set.

name: parse_command_line_args
description: Copies a text block into a newly allocated buffer and splits it into arguments at spaces, tabs and line breaks, treating quoted text as one argument in which a doubled quote stands for one quote. It builds a null-terminated array of pointers to the arguments and stores the count in the data area.

name: copy_limited_string_with_pad
description: Copies up to the given number of bytes from the source, stopping after a zero byte, then fills the rest of the destination with zero bytes. It returns the destination pointer.

name: move_memory_block
description: Copies the given number of bytes from one area to another, choosing the copy direction so that overlapping areas are handled correctly. It returns nothing.

name: append_string_limited
description: Appends the second string to the end of the first, copying at most 32,767 characters and stopping at the source's terminating zero byte. It returns the first string's pointer.

name: append_string_with_count
description: Appends bytes from the second string to the end of the first for at most the given count, and adds a terminating zero byte if the source did not run out.

name: compare_two_byte_strings
description: Compares two byte strings up to a limit of 32,767 characters. It returns minus one if the first string is smaller at the first difference, one if it is larger, and zero if they match.

name: copy_string_to_buffer
description: Copies a zero-terminated string into the destination, including the terminator, and returns the destination pointer.

name: open_icon_library_resource
description: Calls a routine with the name icon.library and stores a library handle and a second value into the structure passed as the first argument. It releases the temporary values before returning.

name: format_text_into_buffer
description: Stores its first argument as the output position in the data area, formats text through a library routine using the second argument and a stack argument, then writes a zero terminator at the end of the output.

name: format_text_into_buffer
description: Stores its first argument as the output position in the data area, formats text through a library routine using the second argument and a stack argument, then writes a zero terminator at the end of the output.

name: append_byte_to_output
description: Writes its byte argument at the current output position in the data area, advances that position by one, and returns the byte.

name: format_number_digits
description: Writes an integer's digits backward into a buffer using a character table in the data area, repeatedly taking remainders and quotients through a routine. It adds a minus sign when the value is negative and the flag is set, and returns the new start of the text.

name: format_printf_style_text
description: Walks a format string, copying literal characters through a callback and handling percent specifiers with optional flags, width, precision and size modifiers. It supports character, string, decimal, unsigned, octal and hexadecimal conversions, and returns the count of characters written or -1 on error.

name: perform_signed_division
description: Divides by working on the magnitudes of two signed inputs: it calls an unsigned division routine, then negates the quotient when the input signs differ. It returns the result together with the second argument as a 64-bit value.

name: negate_remainder_if_negative
description: Calls a division-style routine, then negates the second value it leaves in a register when the first argument is negative, and returns both values together.

name: call_and_return_pair
description: Calls one routine and returns the value it leaves in a register, together with the original second argument, as a 64-bit result.

name: forward_call_and_return
description: Calls one other routine with no arguments and then returns, doing nothing else.

name: divide_unsigned_32bit
description: Divides a 32-bit unsigned value by a 32-bit divisor and returns the quotient and remainder together in one 64-bit result. Divisors above 65535 use a 16-step shift-and-subtract loop, while smaller divisors use direct 16-bit divide steps.

name: measure_string_length
description: Counts the bytes before the terminating zero byte at the start of the given string and returns that count.

name: run_hook_then_forward
description: If a function pointer stored in the data area is set, calls it, then passes the argument to another routine.

name: release_program_resources
description: Releases the stored resources in a fixed order: it frees each entry of a counted list and the list block, calls a function pointer if one is set, and releases three further handles when they are set. It also releases the arrays it allocated earlier, when the related handle is clear.

name: close_table_entry
description: Closes the file handle in a slot of a table when the index is valid, the slot is in use and no flag bit is set, then clears the slot and returns zero. For an invalid index or an empty slot it records error code 2 and returns minus one.

name: multiply_low_32_bits
description: Multiplies two 32-bit inputs using cross products of their 16-bit halves and returns the low 32 bits of the product as the first value, with the second input passed back as the other word.

name: call_close_via_pointer
description: Calls the file-closing routine through a function pointer table entry in the data area, with no arguments, and then returns.

name: call_open_via_pointer
description: Calls the file-opening routine through a function pointer table entry in the data area, with no arguments, and then returns.

name: call_library_base_entry
description: Calls a library function through a pointer table entry at offset minus 414 from the library base stored in the data area, then returns.

name: create_signal_block
description: Obtains a signal number through a routine, then allocates a 34-byte block and fills in its fields from the arguments, the signal number and a value from a second routine. It releases the signal and returns zero if the allocation fails, and otherwise passes the block to a further routine and returns it.

name: release_signal_block
description: Releases a block made by the matching setup routine: if its field at offset 10 is set it passes the block to a routine, clears its status byte and a stored value, passes the stored signal number to a routine, and releases the 34-byte block.

name: call_library_base_entry
description: Calls a library function through a pointer table entry at offset minus 198 from the library base stored in the data area, then returns.

name: call_library_base_entry
description: Calls a library function through a pointer table entry at offset minus 198 from the library base stored in the data area, then returns.

name: call_library_base_entry
description: Calls a library function through a pointer table entry at offset minus 294 from the library base stored in the data area, then returns.

name: call_library_base_entry
description: Calls a library function through a pointer table entry at offset minus 210 from the library base stored in the data area, then returns.

name: call_library_base_entry
description: Calls a library function through a pointer table entry at offset minus 210 from the library base stored in the data area, then returns.

name: initialize_list_header
description: Writes a head pointer four bytes past the start of the block, clears the word that follows it, and stores the block's own address eight bytes in. It sets up a list header inside the given block.

name: call_library_base_entry
description: Calls a library function through a pointer table entry at offset minus 552 from the library base stored in the data area, then returns.

name: call_library_base_entry
description: Calls a library function through a pointer table entry at offset minus 354 from a second library base stored in the data area, then returns.

name: call_library_base_entry
description: Calls a library function through a pointer table entry at offset minus 90 from a second library base stored in the data area, then returns.

name: clear_data_and_start
description: Program entry point: it clears about 34 kilobytes of the data area, saves the stack pointer and the library base in it, calls a library routine if a flag bit is set, and then calls a setup routine or the next routine depending on its result.

name: run_startup_with_memory_check
description: Runs a sequence of setup calls, raising a stage counter after each step. It then compares an available memory value with a fixed threshold, calls a routine with a fixed argument when it is below, and runs an endless loop; the text 'Not enough memory' is referenced.

name: process_game_step
description: Handles one step of the game state: it reads a message code from input, stores either a 33-byte block or a two-byte value depending on that code, and checks board state values before choosing a result code. The text 'Boards are not synchronized' is referenced, and the routine returns a small code that the caller uses for the next state.

name: release_stages_in_reverse
description: Calls a routine and then runs a series of cleanup steps in reverse order, each only when the stage counter has reached its level, finishing with a final call. One of the steps passes two stored values to a routine.

name: release_stages_in_reverse
description: Calls a routine and then runs a series of cleanup steps in reverse order, each only when the stage counter has reached its level, finishing with a final call. One of the steps passes two stored values to a routine.

name: take_pending_buffer_address
description: If a pending flag in the data area is set, calls a routine, clears the flag, calls another routine, and returns the address of a fixed buffer in the data area. Otherwise it returns zero.

name: return_zero_stub
description: Returns zero immediately, with no other work.

name: build_square_state_table
description: Fills a 64-entry table, one entry per square of an 8 by 8 grid, with a state byte built from a per-square lookup and flag bits. It calls routines before and after the loop.

description: Re-enters the square-state fill loop with preset register values, filling the remaining entries of the 64-entry table and returning once the index reaches 64.

name: fill_square_state_entries
description: Fills the 64-entry square-state table, one code per square, using the same lookups as the table builder before it. It returns once the index reaches 64.

name: build_row_masks_for_flag
description: For each of the eight rows, clears a mask byte and sets one bit per square whose state has a piece class and whose flag matches the test argument. The masks are stored in the data area.

name: clear_selected_squares
description: Clears the pending square selection: if the first selection field is set it passes zero to a routine, marks the field unset, and calls another routine. It then marks the second selection field unset.

name: run_board_event_loop
description: Sets four buffer pointers 8000 bytes apart, draws six entries through routines, copies a 480-byte block, and then runs the input-event loop. Event codes 4098, 4099, 12288, 12290 and 12291 each select a different branch of that loop.

name: copy_board_then_run_events
description: Copies 480 bytes from a source buffer into the board table, then runs the input-event loop. Event codes 4098, 4099, 12288, 12290 and 12291 select the branches of that loop.

name: handle_board_events
description: Applies a pending square change, then waits for an input event code and dispatches it. Codes 4098, 4099, 12288, 12290 and 12291 each select a branch that changes the table, leaves the loop, clears the table, copies 480 bytes, or calls a load routine.

name: wait_for_board_load_event
description: Runs the board event loop until a load event (code 12291) is received and its routine reports success, then returns. Other codes are dispatched as in the other loops.

name: handle_board_events
description: Dispatches input events in the board loop after applying any pending square change, with the same branch structure as the other event loops.

name: dispatch_board_events
description: Runs the board input loop once a pending square has been resolved, dispatching event codes 4098, 4099, 12288, 12290 and 12291 to their branches.

name: dispatch_board_events
description: Checks a coordinate range, then runs the board input loop, dispatching event codes 4098, 4099, 12288, 12290 and 12291 to their branches.

name: find_free_slot_or_report
description: Searches a 32-entry table for a free slot. When none is free it shows the 'Too many pieces.' message; otherwise it makes the found slot current and dispatches input events.

name: draw_entry_and_dispatch_events
description: Draws the entry at the index held in a register through a routine, then dispatches input events in the board loop.

name: reset_board_selection_state
description: Resets the selection and board state fields and copies stored values back into the state fields, then returns.

name: dispatch_board_events
description: Dispatches board input events: event codes select the table-change, loop-exit, clear, copy and load branches, and the routine loops until one of them exits.

name: clear_board_and_dispatch
description: Clears the 64-entry board table and its square codes, then continues dispatching input events.

name: restore_board_then_dispatch
description: Copies 480 bytes from a stored board into the board table, clears the pending selection, and continues dispatching input events.

name: finish_board_load
description: Finishes a board load: sets the state fields from stored values, runs the reset and refresh routines, clears the busy flag, and returns.

name: copy_board_bytes
description: Copies 480 bytes from one buffer to another, one byte at a time.

name: wait_for_input_event
description: Repeatedly calls an input routine until it returns a non-zero event code, then returns that code.

name: forward_call_with_argument
description: Calls another routine with its argument and then returns.

name: call_hook_with_argument
description: Calls a function pointer stored in the data area with its argument, then calls another routine with no arguments.

name: map_coordinates_to_square
description: Maps screen coordinates to a board square using two threshold tables of nine entries each. It records the square and, when the selection changes, toggles a flag and calls a routine; coordinates outside the grid clear the selection.

name: reset_pending_square_state
description: Passes the two pending square values to routines, clears them along with the pending selection, and resets two state fields.

name: load_pending_square_state
description: Copies three stored bytes from the data area into state fields, then calls a routine with the argument 28.

name: read_text_entry_line
description: Reads an editable text line into the buffer given as the second argument, showing an underscore cursor, accepting printable characters up to a maximum length, handling backspace, and ending at Return. It returns the final length.

name: prompt_for_thinking_minutes
description: Shows the 'Number of minutes to think:' prompt, reads a decimal number typed by the user, and repeats until the value is between 1 and 10,000. It returns that value.

name: parse_entered_number
description: Converts the typed text into a decimal number and returns it once it is between 1 and 10,000; otherwise it asks again.

name: read_number_entry
description: Reads a line of text, converts its digits to a decimal number, and repeats until the value is between 1 and 10,000. It then returns the number.

name: return_without_action
description: Returns immediately without doing anything.

name: show_message_box_and_wait
description: Draws a message box sized to its text, shows the message with a Left Button prompt, and waits for a specific input event before clearing the box.
